finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection remains valuable after sulfur admission: removal loses 0.128 mean Top-1
finding_summary.insights:
The joint posterior allocation still contributes substantially after sulfur admission changes the available pool and later ancestry. This is now measured under the current gated conditions, with exposure in every task and seed; the earlier ungated loss alone could not establish that. More novel cores, more new parent-beating cores and easier selected-stream prediction did not preserve absolute source quality or incumbent improvement. This rules out treating those local proxies, or the narrower seed-average dispersion, as sufficient evidence of useful exploration. The result concerns the whole successful allocation consumer and its total adaptive effect. It does not isolate a mean, fingerprint, normalization or residual constituent, show a sulfur interaction, or attribute the whole graph foundation.

Chemistry remains mixed. Fewer N-halogen structures coexist with more O-halogen and peroxide structures, while useful conventional ether/ketone and methoxy alternatives and useful permitted sulfur remain. Some of the highest labels still belong to chemically doubtful output, including the cyclic-peroxide family in the sole improving endpoint. Those examples preserve exceptions without proving a chemical mediator, a universal liability penalty or a benefit from broader filtering. Passive alternatives have no new labels or continued ancestry. Current composition review, separate constituent and joint-interaction evidence, chemical mediation, partial alternative-lineage composition and full-history coverage remain open.
finding_summary.results:
All fifteen matched task/seed runs completed with the full budget. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.468270, a paired loss of 0.128183. All three seed averages fell, by 0.20602, 0.07253 and 0.10599. Fourteen endpoints fell; the sole gain was zaleplon seed 1, from 0.474117 to 0.479919. The control emitted exactly the first ten admitted molecules from every one of 435 complete 160-member pools. The passive original selector chose a different set in every batch and strictly preferred another identity in 4321 of 4350 same-mask selections. There were no natural fallback, incomplete-pool or factorization failures. The entire original GP computation and sulfur rule remained present.

The control produced 634 parent-beating offspring versus 648, but only 155 sequential incumbent advances versus 255. Its average offspring score was 0.22594 versus 0.37205, and average best-generating-parent score 0.31170 versus 0.45530. It created more new typed/generic cores (2366/1815 versus 1820/1117), including more new parent-beating cores (325/229 versus 262/163). Fewer accepted sources later entered breeding (2038 versus 2469). Final-batch sources were censored for later reuse. Prospective prediction accuracy on the control's own accepted stream was better: unequal-label pair accuracy 0.771 versus 0.710 and mean within-batch Spearman 0.666 versus 0.526. Those are different selected streams; at the same actual identity the passive original mean is unchanged and its MSE contrast is zero.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive bonds, difficult connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry across divergent seed histories
molecular.overall_character: Node n-605c7a785b51 produces linked nitrile/azaaryl amines, fused aryl amides, large azaaryl/dicarbonyl assemblies, aryl cyclic amines and sulfoxides, connected nitrogen/dione rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Whole-trajectory diversity is moderate, with much narrower repeated leader families within seeds; distinct strings are not evidence of independent useful scaffolds. Digest ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9437-0.9747 and aromatic-string incidence 0.6609-0.9724. These are fractions of molecules exhibiting text features, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Charged and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on all five objectives. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2112 of 4350 Child optimizer observations, compared with 2455 Parent observations. Child has 397 observations with O-O bonds, 172 with N-halogen bonds, 517 with O-halogen bonds and 27 with S-halogen bonds; Parent counts are respectively 128, 786, 217 and 93. Sulfur-containing observations remain 1108 Child versus 1100 Parent; permitted local sulfur chemistry is not a whole-molecule plausibility guarantee. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and drug-likeness weak because recognizable medicinal motifs coexist with reactive local attachments, difficult ring geometry, tiny fragments and overgrown structures. All 15 Child and 15 authoritative published Parent trajectories were read completely. Each side has 900 records per objective, including 870 accepted optimizer observations; no path, task or paired seed is missing. All digest counters, counts, extreme scores and digest molecule/score/evaluation/source/seed tuples match the Child files. context.comparison has child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0/1/2 and no profile mismatch. Full trajectories establish seed endpoints; digest final_molecules are late proposals, not incumbents. The measured macro values are Child 0.4682702139687083 and Parent 0.59645311428869, with paired delta -0.12818290031998167. Chemistry differences are own-stream descriptive associations under divergent feedback histories, not selector activation, a selector constituent contribution, a sulfur contribution or chemical mediation. Unlabelled passive pool alternatives have no invented score or ancestry here. The frozen catalog composition_status=needs_review at v-17b4d64669a7955c8e61ca7e remains unresolved by this report; whole-foundation, constituent, joint-interaction, mediation, partial L07 composition and full-history-processing gaps remain separate. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection remains valuable after sulfur admission: removal loses 0.128 mean Top-1
finding_summary.insights:
The joint posterior allocation still contributes substantially after sulfur admission changes the available pool and later ancestry. This is now measured under the current gated conditions, with exposure in every task and seed; the earlier ungated loss alone could not establish that. More novel cores, more new parent-beating cores and easier selected-stream prediction did not preserve absolute source quality or incumbent improvement. This rules out treating those local proxies, or the narrower seed-average dispersion, as sufficient evidence of useful exploration. The result concerns the whole successful allocation consumer and its total adaptive effect. It does not isolate a mean, fingerprint, normalization or residual constituent, show a sulfur interaction, or attribute the whole graph foundation.

Chemistry remains mixed. Fewer N-halogen structures coexist with more O-halogen and peroxide structures, while useful conventional ether/ketone and methoxy alternatives and useful permitted sulfur remain. Some of the highest labels still belong to chemically doubtful output, including the cyclic-peroxide family in the sole improving endpoint. Those examples preserve exceptions without proving a chemical mediator, a universal liability penalty or a benefit from broader filtering. Passive alternatives have no new labels or continued ancestry. Current composition review, separate constituent and joint-interaction evidence, chemical mediation, partial alternative-lineage composition and full-history coverage remain open.
finding_summary.results:
All fifteen matched task/seed runs completed with the full budget. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.468270, a paired loss of 0.128183. All three seed averages fell, by 0.20602, 0.07253 and 0.10599. Fourteen endpoints fell; the sole gain was zaleplon seed 1, from 0.474117 to 0.479919. The control emitted exactly the first ten admitted molecules from every one of 435 complete 160-member pools. The passive original selector chose a different set in every batch and strictly preferred another identity in 4321 of 4350 same-mask selections. There were no natural fallback, incomplete-pool or factorization failures. The entire original GP computation and sulfur rule remained present.

The control produced 634 parent-beating offspring versus 648, but only 155 sequential incumbent advances versus 255. Its average offspring score was 0.22594 versus 0.37205, and average best-generating-parent score 0.31170 versus 0.45530. It created more new typed/generic cores (2366/1815 versus 1820/1117), including more new parent-beating cores (325/229 versus 262/163). Fewer accepted sources later entered breeding (2038 versus 2469). Final-batch sources were censored for later reuse. Prospective prediction accuracy on the control's own accepted stream was better: unequal-label pair accuracy 0.771 versus 0.710 and mean within-batch Spearman 0.666 versus 0.526. Those are different selected streams; at the same actual identity the passive original mean is unchanged and its MSE contrast is zero.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection remains valuable after sulfur admission: removal loses 0.128 mean Top-1
finding_summary.insights:
The joint posterior allocation still contributes substantially after sulfur admission changes the available pool and later ancestry. This is now measured under the current gated conditions, with exposure in every task and seed; the earlier ungated loss alone could not establish that. More novel cores, more new parent-beating cores and easier selected-stream prediction did not preserve absolute source quality or incumbent improvement. This rules out treating those local proxies, or the narrower seed-average dispersion, as sufficient evidence of useful exploration. The result concerns the whole successful allocation consumer and its total adaptive effect. It does not isolate a mean, fingerprint, normalization or residual constituent, show a sulfur interaction, or attribute the whole graph foundation.

Chemistry remains mixed. Fewer N-halogen structures coexist with more O-halogen and peroxide structures, while useful conventional ether/ketone and methoxy alternatives and useful permitted sulfur remain. Some of the highest labels still belong to chemically doubtful output, including the cyclic-peroxide family in the sole improving endpoint. Those examples preserve exceptions without proving a chemical mediator, a universal liability penalty or a benefit from broader filtering. Passive alternatives have no new labels or continued ancestry. Current composition review, separate constituent and joint-interaction evidence, chemical mediation, partial alternative-lineage composition and full-history coverage remain open.
finding_summary.results:
All fifteen matched task/seed runs completed with the full budget. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.468270, a paired loss of 0.128183. All three seed averages fell, by 0.20602, 0.07253 and 0.10599. Fourteen endpoints fell; the sole gain was zaleplon seed 1, from 0.474117 to 0.479919. The control emitted exactly the first ten admitted molecules from every one of 435 complete 160-member pools. The passive original selector chose a different set in every batch and strictly preferred another identity in 4321 of 4350 same-mask selections. There were no natural fallback, incomplete-pool or factorization failures. The entire original GP computation and sulfur rule remained present.

The control produced 634 parent-beating offspring versus 648, but only 155 sequential incumbent advances versus 255. Its average offspring score was 0.22594 versus 0.37205, and average best-generating-parent score 0.31170 versus 0.45530. It created more new typed/generic cores (2366/1815 versus 1820/1117), including more new parent-beating cores (325/229 versus 262/163). Fewer accepted sources later entered breeding (2038 versus 2469). Final-batch sources were censored for later reuse. Prospective prediction accuracy on the control's own accepted stream was better: unequal-label pair accuracy 0.771 versus 0.710 and mean within-batch Spearman 0.666 versus 0.526. Those are different selected streams; at the same actual identity the passive original mean is unchanged and its MSE contrast is zero.
